title: Time plan card

intro: Lesson 47: Section A timed: planning the three hours and Text One (Q1 to Q3). Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

passage.title: Text One, 'Why I Walk' (teacher-written modern column for TGA)
paras: Three years ago I sold my car. Friends assumed I had lost my job or my mind. In fact, I had simply noticed that I was spending forty minutes a day in traffic, shouting at strangers through glass.

Now I walk the two miles to work. It takes longer, of course: thirty-five minutes in good weather, forty when the rain comes sideways off the river. But those minutes are mine. I have learned the names of the streets I used to blur past. I know which bakery opens first, which tree flowers earliest in spring, which corner smells of coffee and which of wet dogs.
Walking has not made me fitter overnight; it has made me slower, and slowness turns out to be a kind of wealth. When I arrive at my desk, my head is clear.
I am not telling you to sell your car. I am asking you to try, once a week, arriving somewhere on your own two feet. You may find, as I did, that the journey was the point.

panels.title: Today's Text One questions
points: Q1: From paragraph 1, give one reason the writer sold the car. (1)
Q2: How long does the walk take in good weather? (1)
Q3: How do language and structure show the benefits of walking? (10)

keywords.def: how many minutes each section gets
how a text is organised and develops
what a choice makes the reader think or feel

questions.a: Q1: they spent forty minutes a day in traffic (or were shouting at strangers through glass). Q2: thirty-five minutes.

questions.q: Core (timed, 15 minutes): in the portal response box, answer Q3. Starter: 'The writer presents walking as...'
questions.a: Mark scheme points: list of sensory details ('bakery', 'coffee', 'wet dogs') shows noticing; metaphor 'slowness... a kind of wealth'; contrast of traffic anger with clear head; structure from past (car) to present (walking) to direct appeal; final line 'the journey was the point' as a reflective ending. Top answers weave language and structure with effects.

questions.q: Self-mark Q3 with the mark scheme points; add one missing point.
Stretch: write the structural point you missed in one sentence.
questions.a: For example: The final direct appeal turns a personal story into advice for the reader.

questions.q: Which is the best Q1 answer?
options: They spent forty minutes a day in traffic.
Because cars are bad for the planet and expensive and they wanted to walk.
questions.a: B) They spent forty minutes a day in traffic.. It is precise and from paragraph 1; the second is invented; the third is what friends wrongly assumed.

questions.q: In the time plan, Section A gets about...
Answer the ponder in one sentence.
questions.a: About 1.8 minutes a mark: so a 1-mark question gets under two minutes.
